pick.name: Cal.com (Free cloud)
pick.why: Free forever for 1 user: unlimited event types and calendars, Stripe/PayPal payments, free Attio app (bookings sync into the CRM pick), embeds
pick.free_limits: Free: 1 user, unlimited event types, templated workflows only, Cal.com branding; Teams USD 12/user/mo

alts.name: Google Calendar appointment schedules (via Google AI Pro)
alts.why: Already paid until Jan 2028: premium appointment scheduling (multiple schedules, reminders, multi-calendar checks per Google); payments tier unclear
alts.free_limits: Premium features while AI Pro lasts; free accounts get one booking page

alts.name: Calendly
alts.why: Buyers know it; but free is 1 event type
alts.free_limits: Free: 1 event type, 1 calendar; Standard USD 10/seat

candidates.name: Google appointment schedules
candidates.verdict: Good while AI Pro lasts; no CRM sync or payments

candidates.name: Cal.diy self-host
candidates.verdict: MIT community fork, missing teams/workflows; 'personal, non-production' per README

decision: Use Cal.com Free cloud for ALL scheduling (sales calls and customer-discovery interviews). It is production-grade; only the self-host route changed (closed source since 15 Apr 2026; public repo is the MIT Cal.diy fork, flagged non-production). Google appointment schedules (premium via AI Pro until Jan 2028) is the fallback.
note: Consolidated: this same Cal.com account also handles customer interviews (Discover track). Sync it to Attio, the CRM pick, through Cal.com's free Attio app.
details: Licence change flagged 2026: Cal.com production code private; GitHub repo now Cal.diy (MIT).

verify.note: Cal.com Free confirmed: 1 user, unlimited event types/calendars, templated workflows, Stripe+PayPal, HubSpot/Salesforce two-way sync; Teams USD 12. Closed-source date confirmed: the 'refactor: Cal.diy' commit landed 2026-04-15 and calcom/cal.com now redirects to calcom/cal.diy (MIT, 'non-production'), whose README tells commercial users to use Cal.com cloud, so cloud Free is fine for production. Fix the 'why': the CRM pick is Attio, not HubSpot. Cal.com's App Store has a free Attio app that syncs bookings into Attio, which is the relevant point. Cal.com changed its ToS/DPA/Privacy on 1 Nov 2026 (changelog v6.9.5); skim it.
